name: Lydia
overview: Lydia is a female figure known from the New Testament, specifically identified as being from Thyatira and engaged in the trade of purple fabrics. Her role as a seller of purple cloth marks her as a person of some means and influence within her community. Beyond these details, Scripture provides limited additional personal information about her.
namesAndTitles: The only recorded name for this individual is Lydia, which is a proper name mentioned in Acts 16:14. There is no special meaning or divine origin indicated for her name in the biblical text.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture does not record family relationships for Lydia beyond what is indicated by her occupation and place of origin. No specific familial connections are noted in the biblical account.
scriptureSignificance: Lydia's significance in the biblical narrative lies in her identification as a businesswoman from Thyatira who sold purple fabrics, a luxury item in the ancient world. Her mention in Acts 16:14 highlights her as a notable convert to the Christian faith, representing the early spread of the gospel among Gentile populations. Her example underscores the inclusivity of the Christian message and the role of women in the early church.
